samples.summary: Cross-sheet grid resolver rebuilds the full merge cover map on every formula cell, so a budget-legal merge map is an attacker-controlled work amplifier
samples.evidence:
The rewritten resolver calls `buildMergeCoverMap(Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {}))` inline (sheet-view.tsx:1242) with no memoization. The resolver is invoked from `Sheet.fetchGridByReferences` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3323), which is called from `calculateCell` -> `fetchGridByReferences` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:95), and `calculate` (calculator.ts:41-47) runs that once **per formula cell** in the recalc set. `buildMergeCoverMap` is bounded by `MaxMergeCoveredCells = 1,000,000` (merging.ts:42) *per build*, not across builds.

Attack: any principal holding `rw` on the document (the Yorkie auth webhook authorizes by (document, verb) and never inspects op content, as this PR's own doc text states) — or any API key with write scope via `PUT .../merges`, which accepts up to 1e6 covered cells — writes a legal 1e6-cell merge map onto tab `S2`. A second tab holding N formula cells that reference `S2!...` then costs N x 1e6 Map insertions on every recalculation (every remote change / every commit), synchronously on the main thread. N=1000 is ~1e9 insertions: the tab stops painting for **every** collaborator who opens the document, repeatedly, and the state is stored so it recurs on every open.

The engine's own reader does not have this shape: `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:876-882) builds once and caches into `this.mergeCoverMap`. The new comment at sheet-view.tsx:1236-1241 asserts this walk is "spent against the same budget `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` spends", which reads as covering a cost the budget does not actually bound here. Fix: hoist the cover map out of the resolver and cache it per (tabId, merges-version), as the engine does.

samples.summary: Resolver reads the raw Yorkie merge map with bare `Object.entries` instead of the repo's `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`, so a duplicate-own-keys proxy error throws out of formula evaluation
samples.evidence:
sheet-view.tsx:1243 does `Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {}) as Array<[Sref, MergeSpan]>` directly on the Yorkie proxy. The repo has a dedicated guard for exactly this hazard: `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:47-61) catches the `TypeError: ... ownKeys ... duplicate` a Yorkie object proxy can raise and falls back to a `toJSON` snapshot. Every backend reader of the same field uses it (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:152-154, 193; worksheet.controller.ts:122; worksheet-structure.ts:279, 601, 694).

Attack/exposure: a collaborator's concurrent writes to `ws.merges` (or a deliberately crafted op from any `rw` client) produce a merge map whose proxy `ownKeys` trap reports duplicates. `Object.entries` then throws inside `setGridResolver`, which propagates out of `fetchGridByReferences` -> `calculateCell` -> `calculate`, breaking recalculation for every viewer of the referencing tab. The delta explicitly rewrote this line in the name of defensive reading of the raw CRDT map (comment at lines 1236-1241) but left the one documented CRDT-read hazard unguarded.

samples.summary: New `moveStraddlingFreeze` walks attacker-writable merge entries with unguarded `parseRef` and unvalidated spans, unlike the `buildMergeCoverMap`/`isCountableMergeSpan` hardening added in the same change
samples.evidence:
`moveStraddlingFreeze` (merging.ts:495-504) does `parseRef(anchorSref)` with no try/catch and uses `span.rs`/`span.cs` with no `isCountableMergeSpan` check, while the sibling function added in the same commit (`buildMergeCoverMap`, merging.ts:179-194) does both and documents why. The backend hands it the raw CRDT map: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` passes `safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges ?? {})` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:193), which filters nothing — it only guards against duplicate-key proxy errors.

Vector: a `rw` collaborator writes `ws.merges["notaref"] = {rs:2,cs:2}` directly through Yorkie (auth webhook does not inspect op content). `parseRef("notaref")` throws (coordinates.ts:350-352) inside `doc.update`, rolling the update back and surfacing a 500 on `POST .../move` for every other caller. A non-integer span (`rs: "x"`) makes `moveMerge` produce NaN, so `crossesFreezePane` compares against NaN and silently returns false — the freeze guard fails open for that entry.

Impact is bounded because `assertMoveKeepsMerges` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:152-163) already `parseRef`s every key one line earlier and throws first, so the malformed-key 500 is pre-existing rather than newly introduced; I could not find a path where `moveStraddlingFreeze` is the first to touch a hostile key. Reporting for completeness of the hardening the delta set out to do.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: sheet-view.tsx:1242 calls buildMergeCoverMap inline inside the setGridResolver callback (registered at sheet-view.tsx:1220) with no memoization — a grep for useMemo/coverToAnchor across packages/frontend/src shows this is the only occurrence and it is uncached. The resolver is invoked from Sheet.fetchGridByReferences (sheet.ts:3321-3329), which calculator.ts:95 calls inside the per-cell loop of calculate (calculator.ts:41-47), so the map is rebuilt once per formula cell in the recalc set. buildMergeCoverMap creates a fresh budget per call (merging.ts:174) and admits up to MaxMergeCoveredCells = 1,000,000 covered cells (merging.ts:42, spent at merging.ts:176-206), so the cap bounds each build, not the aggregate — exactly as the finding states. The engine's own reader does cache (Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap, sheet.ts:876-883 stores into this.mergeCoverMap), confirming the asymmetry. The merge map is an attacker-writable plain CRDT field by the code's own admission (merging.ts:146-154), so any rw principal can persist a budget-legal 1e6-cell map plus N cross-sheet formula cells and impose N x 1e6 synchronous Map insertions on every collaborator on every recalc/open. No guard, throttle, or cache elsewhere makes this unreachable, so I have no ground to refute.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed: sheet-view.tsx:1243 calls `Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {})` on the raw Yorkie proxy obtained at line 1233, while the repo's guard `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` (worksheet-record.ts:47-61) exists and is used by every other reader of `ws.merges` (yorkie-store.ts:977,1072,1277,1291,1309; worksheet-structure.ts:279,601,694; worksheet.controller.ts:122; worksheet-structure.controller.ts:152,193). So the finding is factually accurate and a real robustness defect. However, it is out of scope for the Security lens. The described impact is a `TypeError` escaping a client-side formula resolver, breaking recalculation in a viewer's browser. No authorization gate is added, weakened, or bypassed (the resolver runs purely client-side on a document the viewer already has open); no secret or sensitive data is exposed; the "crafted op" does not flow into any SQL/command/path/template sink, so it is not injection; no crypto, signature, HMAC, or comparison logic is involved; and it is not SSRF, unsafe deserialization, or path traversal. The premised actor must already hold `rw` rights and the only effect is an exception in a peer's renderer, i.e. a general logic/robustness bug that this rubric explicitly routes to the correctness lens. The repository confirms that ownership: the identical finding is already filed under .agent-review/correctness/summary.md:10 and .agent-review/correctness/verdict.json:20-21, not under a security stage. Refuted on lane scope only, not on the facts.
